prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere). Ground segment plans, acquires, keeps ops safe, generates/archives products, controlled service access. Outside boundary: spacecraft, launch segment, external user processing. Parts: Mission Control Center (alias Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands; owns contact schedule; primary routing policy point; each contact = readiness check, live monitoring, post-pass closure. Flight Dynamics Facility (alias Mistral): orbit, maneuvers; visibility predictions/antenna pointing to planning. Payload Processing Facility: processing, calibration, staging; coordinates Primary (nominal)/Backup (failover, lower routing preference, paths routinely tested) Processing Clusters. Network Control System (alias Lantern): comms monitoring, routing; station allocations, antenna readiness, contact start/end; authoritative WAN state; confirms timing alarms not maintenance/failed local check before forwarding to Spacecraft Ops Team. Mission Planning System: plans; receives contact booking requests. Command Validation Gateway: shall rule-check commands. Telemetry Ingest Service. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report per pass. Product Quality Service; Long Term Archive (authoritative; PPC->LTA transfers rate-limited during contacts); User Services Portal. Ground Network Manager (alias Juniper): antenna availability, arbitration; Antenna Deicing Notice; pins paths before AOS; on latency breach checks carrier, then routing, loss, queues, security delays before declaring mission impact; coordinates with Cybersecurity Desk before blocking traffic in contingency. Antennas: North/South S-Band (protected routers to MCC); Kiruna/Svalbard X-Band (dual WAN to PPF); validate time vs local references before contact. Teams: Spacecraft Ops, Flight Dynamics (monitors timing quality vs clock bias), Payload Calibration, Cybersecurity Desk (sends Security Exception Ticket for baseline deviation). Timing: redundant reference clocks at MCC and FDF with holdover; PTP in data centers/enclaves; authenticated NTP elsewhere. Security monitoring per site (sensors, endpoint, privileged logging, compliance) reviewed each shift; correlation on route advertisements, auth failures, remote access, encrypted volume. Rules: daily cut-off; priority safety>timeliness>efficiency; X-band rain downgrade; S-band unavailable high wind; authenticated routing, no ad hoc changes during contacts; admin networks unadvertised; latency budgets per class.

New part:
S078: The North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna are normally assigned for command and low-rate telemetry contacts, while the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna support high-rate telemetry reception when the visibility geometry and data volume justify their use.
S079: The Network Control System provides the Mission Control Center with antenna status, link configuration, timing references, and routing readiness before each pass begins.
S080: The Telemetry Ingest Service accepts real-time frames, validates basic framing and time continuity, and records reception metadata needed for later operational review.
S081: The Telemetry Ingest Service produces the Pass Replay Packet after a contact when the received stream must be reconstructed for engineering review.
S082: During live operations, the Spacecraft Operations Team monitors spacecraft mode, power state, thermal margins, attitude indicators, command counters, onboard storage, and fault protection messages from the Mission Control Center consoles.
S083: Console displays emphasize deviations from expected state rather than raw parameter volume, because operators must identify safety trends while a contact is still available.
S084: The console lead is responsible for declaring pass status, authorizing planned command execution through the Command Validation Gateway, and pausing the activity when telemetry does not match the expected configuration.
S085: The telemetry engineer verifies reception quality, frame loss, latency, and stream continuity, and advises the console lead when degraded link conditions could affect command confidence.
S086: The spacecraft systems engineer interprets health telemetry, confirms that subsystem states remain within flight rules, and records any anomaly context needed by subsystem specialists.
S087: The Ground Network Manager remains accountable for antenna assignment, ground link availability, and coordination with site operations when weather, equipment status, or routing issues affect a contact.
S088: The Flight Dynamics Team uses tracking measurements and validated time tags from the contact to support orbit assessment at the Flight Dynamics Facility.
S089: The Orbit Determination Engine supports routine state updates and provides the basis for predicting future visibility periods, maneuver planning constraints, and antenna pointing expectations.
S090: Pass reconstruction begins when the contact closes and combines command history, received telemetry timing, ground station status, and operator log entries into a single operational narrative.
S091: The reconstructed pass record is used to confirm whether planned objectives were completed, whether any onboard event occurred outside the timeline, and whether additional engineering analysis is required.
S092: The Payload Processing Facility is also known operationally as Forgehouse in console discussions and shift logs.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
